transcribed_from: Client (student) decisions of 2026-10-09 on the area logic of spaceplan (project docs spaceplan_FOS_investigacion.md and spaceplan_FOT_investigacion.md). Editable: change a value here, or override it per run (CLI --fos, --fos-base, --fot-source, --fot, --floors-policy, --optimum-policy).
verification_note: Design variables, not code. verified=true means the client set them. In RS-1-7 the SDMC has no general lot coverage (only 50 percent on steep-hillside premises, 131.0445(a)); the design FOS is the client's footprint cap. The FOT follows the SDMC (131.0446, Table 131-04J) by default; a fixed FOT is a scenario and its results are marked non-normative.

parameters.counts: enclosed building and garage footprint, measured to the outer face of exterior walls (SDMC 113.0240)
parameters.excludes: decks, open porches, stoops, terraces and stairways (113.0240(a)-(b)), garden and paving

text: Design occupancy (FOS): the ground footprint of the house (interior and garage) may cover at most this fraction of the base area; base 'envelope' = area inside the required setbacks, 'lot' = lot area (the SDMC and Colombian convention).

parameters.fixed_note: Scenario value from RT-type zones (townhouses), not RS-1-7: results with source 'fixed' exceed the SDMC FAR by about 42 percent on the pilot and are marked non-normative.

text: Construction factor (FOT): 'sdmc' applies SDMC 131.0446 (Table 131-04J by lot area, hillside rule (a)(2)); 'fixed' replaces it by fixed_value as a scenario.

parameters.note: one_floor_first: a second floor is built only when the program does not fit in one floor within the design footprint and the FOT allows it; 'score' keeps the step-6.6 ranking by household-weighted score.

text: A second floor exists only if the program does not fit on the ground floor and the construction factor allows it.

parameters.note: Minimum of the lot: a basic one-bedroom house (reference, same for every household); minimum of the household: its required program. Optimum 'footprint': the largest program on the household's expansion curve that fits one floor within the design footprint ('knee' keeps the step-6.5d quality-cost knee as a lens). Maximum: 100 percent of the effective FOT, capped by the floors the height allows times the design footprint.

text: Profiles: lot minimum (one bedroom) and household minimum; optimum at the design footprint on one floor; maximum at 100 percent of the FOT.
